prose:
Scott Aaronson reacts to a wave of claimed complexity-theory results, especially OpenAI's matrix-multiplication lower bound, and describes a change in his personal expectations about AI-assisted mathematics. He distinguishes his confidence in the labs' formal artifacts from his much lower confidence in specific cryptographic rumors.

This is expert commentary and a first-person reaction, not an independent proof audit of every cited manuscript. Aaronson says in a comment that he has not read far into the recent papers. His working presumption of correctness and prediction that P versus NP may be near remain his judgments; they do not establish a Boolean separation, a broken cryptosystem or universal verification. This newer post is not the older Reingold-message article that the detector matched by headline similarity.
highlights: Post discusses newly circulated mathematical manuscripts
Matrix-exponent result is central to the reaction
Author expresses personal confidence, not a full proof review
Comment says he has not read far into the papers
No P versus NP proof is established
No cryptosystem failure is verified here
